ABOUT
THE PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a concerning historical condition.
In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

(5) The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women into regional development planning, which is set forth in planning and budget documents covering the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Plan (RPJMD), Strategic Plan of Regional Apparatus Work Units (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Work Plan and Budget of Regional Apparatus Work Units (RKA SKPD).
(6) The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women shall be facilitated by the work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women in the region in coordination with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 3
The objectives of the Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to fulfill their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

Article 14
(1) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the regions is carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.
(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.
(3) The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

ABOUT
THE PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a concerning historical condition.
In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the administration of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relations between women and men that results in suffering or hardship for women including children whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.
11. Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory impairment.

5.8.rationale: The Indonesian regulation does engage the private sector explicitly through obligations on “Perusahaan” (companies). Pasal 8 discusses equal opportunity and equal treatment by companies (“perlakuan yang sama dari Perusahaan”), and Pasal 9 states: “Perusahaan yang menggunakan tenaga kerja perempuan, wajib memberikan perlindungan...” (companies employing women must provide protection), with details to be regulated by a Regent Regulation. However, none of the retrieved candidate passages for this indicator included Pasal 8–9; they focused on community participation and general non-government actors. Because the relevant private-sector engagement evidence exists in the source but was not retrieved, the judge reasonably answered “No” based on what they saw.

7.2.rationale: The Indonesian funding clause (Pasal 23 ayat (2)) states: “Dalam hal daerah mendapatkan bantuan pendanaan ... dari Pemerintah ...” which in Indonesian legal drafting typically refers to the central/national government (“Pemerintah” vs “Pemerintah Daerah”). This is an explicit acknowledgement of possible funding assistance from the (central) Government, in addition to APBD in ayat (1). The retrieved English passage matches this meaning, and the judge’s “Yes” is supported. Therefore the golden label “No” appears wrong.
